REGISTERED ESTABLISHMENT
EXPORT REGISTRATION RECORD
1. Establishment Details
2. Registered Export Operations

This establishment is registered to conduct export operations for wheat (grain). All export activities carried out at this premises are within the registered scope as approved by the Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry (DAFF).
3. Registration Status

Registration RE-VIC-2021-0055 is current and active. The establishment was granted registration on 2 February 2021 and the current registration period extends to 1 February 2024. There are no conditions, suspensions or reviews attached to this registration.
4. Fit and Proper Person

Donna Sheridan is the nominated responsible person for this registration. The establishment has been under continuous management since 2012. The entity is a family trust registered with ASIC. The responsible person has completed the DAFF Export Compliance Fundamentals training and holds current industry accreditation.
5. Registered Premises — Area Description

The registered premises comprise Lot 18 on Plan DP 145604, located at 44 Western Highway, Nhill VIC 3418. The total registered area is 38.4 hectares. The registered boundary is delineated on the attached site plan (Appendix A) and includes all receival, storage, processing and dispatch infrastructure. Adjoining land parcels and access roads are excluded from the registered area.
6. Features, Facilities and Adjoining Sites
6.1 Buildings and Structures
6.2 Services and Utilities
6.3 Adjoining Sites

The registered premises adjoin: (north) sealed public road; (east) cropping paddocks under same ownership; (south) state forest reserve — no stock or chemical activities; (west) neighbour's mixed-farming property — grain growing, no spray operations within 200 m.
7. Layout and Product Flow

The establishment handles wheat through standard receival, storage and dispatch infrastructure. Equipment includes conveyors, augers and an outloading hopper. All operations are conducted within the farm site.
8. Construction, Equipment and Facilities

The establishment infrastructure is designed and maintained to support the export of wheat. Total storage capacity is approximately 3,500 tonnes. Structures are of steel-frame construction with concrete flooring throughout the grain-contact areas. Maintenance inspections are carried out annually and records held on site.
9. Notification of Changes

No changes to the registered establishment name, address, ownership, management or trading name have occurred since the last registration renewal. Should any such changes occur, DAFF will be notified in writing within the required timeframe as per Rule 4-6 of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.
10. Alterations to Registered Premises

No structural alterations or additions to the registered premises have been carried out since the last registration approval. Any proposed alterations will be submitted to DAFF for approval prior to commencement of works, in accordance with Rule 4-5 of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.

The following requirements apply to export consignments destined for UAE:

Phytosanitary Security Procedure

13. Food Safety Program

A HACCP-based food safety program is maintained for all export operations. The program addresses pre-harvest, receival, storage, processing and dispatch stages. Critical control points are documented with monitoring procedures and corrective action plans. The food safety program is reviewed annually or following any significant operational change.
14. Record Keeping

Records relating to all export operations, including receival dockets, storage logs, treatment records, dispatch documentation and audit reports, are maintained on site and in the business management system. Records are retained for a minimum of two years from the date of the relevant export activity in accordance with Rule 4-7B of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.

Establishment: King Island Dairies & Grains Pty Ltd
Address: 33 Station Road, Western Australia
Commodity: Wheat (ASW, APW), Barley (Feed/Malt)

Scope: Receival, drying, storage, cleaning/grading, sampling and bulk loading of wheat and barley for export under the Export Control Act 2020. Applicable to all export-grade grain handled within registered area RE-NSW-3051.
Intended use: Malt-grade barley for malting/brewing industry. APW1/ASW wheat for milling. Consuming population: general adult population. Destination: Japan, Vietnam.

7. Pest Control (Checking Point 3.2)

[DEFICIENCY — NOT DOCUMENTED]
No formal pest control program is documented for King Island Dairies & Grains Pty Ltd. No bait station map, monitoring schedule, contractor engagement or corrective action procedures are included.
8. Traceability and Integrity (Checking Point 4.1)

Traceability System (GCE-TRACE-001):
• One step back: each silo assigned a unique ID containing grower name, paddock ID, variety, harvest year (e.g., GCE-SILO3-SMITH-PADD2-APW1-2025).
• One step forward: each dispatch docket links silo ID → transport unit rego → receiving establishment.
• Batch records: receival docket → lab test result → silo allocation → fumigation certificate → dispatch docket, all linked by lot reference.
• Records retained 2 years minimum. Digital copies in FarmWizard grain management system.
9. Product Flow Chart and Failed Goods (Checking Point 4.1)
Product flow chart: see Section 3 Process Flow Diagram.

[DEFICIENCY — NOT DOCUMENTED]
No formal failed goods procedure for King Island Dairies & Grains Pty Ltd. No documented process for segregation, re-testing, downgrade, destruction or DAFF notification.
10. Phytosanitary Security / Contamination Risk (Checking Point 4.2)

[DEFICIENCY — NOT DOCUMENTED]
No phytosanitary security section in this HACCP plan for King Island Dairies & Grains Pty Ltd. No controls to prevent re-contamination or re-infestation between inspection and dispatch.
11. Verification and Record Keeping
Internal audit of HACCP plan: annual, by HACCP team lead.
External audit: DAFF registered establishment audit (periodic).
CCP monitoring records retained minimum 2 years.
HACCP plan reviewed following: product change, process change, new hazard identified, customer complaint, DAFF non-conformance.

FARM MANAGEMENT PLAN
Registered Establishment — Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021
1. OVERVIEW

Nhill Grain Services is a registered export establishment located at 44 Western Highway, Nhill VIC 3418, VIC. The establishment holds RE Number RE-VIC-2021-0055 and is registered to handle and export Rice under the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021. This Farm Management Plan documents the physical infrastructure, equipment, facilities, design standards, waste management arrangements and establishment condition relevant to compliance with Chapter 4 of the Rules and the DAFF Performance Standards IMLS-12-3742.
2. BUILDINGS AND INFRASTRUCTURE
Rules s4-2 — buildings, equipment, facilities and services required for export operations
3. EQUIPMENT AND MACHINERY
Rules s4-2(4) — equipment adequate for the type of export operations conducted
4. FACILITIES AND SERVICES
Rules s4-2 — Element 2.1 checking points C1, C2, C3
4.1 Buildings, Equipment and Facilities (C1)

The establishment has all buildings, equipment, facilities and services required for the registered export operations. Facilities are maintained in an operational condition appropriate for handling and exporting Rice.
4.2 Lighting (C2)

T5 LED fluorescent panels on 600 mm spacing — 550 lux at floor level throughout processing area. Task lighting above grading line at 600 lux. Loading dock: 400 W LED floods at 418 lux. Emergency lighting on dedicated UPS circuit.
4.3 Handwashing and Toilet Facilities (C3)

Self-contained amenities unit: 2 flush toilets, urinal, 3 hand basins — hot/cold water, liquid soap dispensers, paper towels, hand sanitiser. Sited at main processing entry (<15 m from packing line). Additional wash station at grading line head-of-line position.
5. DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION STANDARDS
Rules s4-2(5), s4-2(6) — Element 2.2 checking points C4, C5, C6
5.1 Cleanability (C4)

Floors: smooth-trowelled reinforced concrete with penetrating sealant (applied 2009, resealed 2014); coved floor-wall junctions throughout. Wall cladding: 1.6 mm Zincalume on galvanised rails to 3.0 m — smooth, washable. All service penetrations sealed with flexible polyurethane. Drain covers: lift-out stainless-steel.
5.2 Contamination and Pest Harbourage Minimisation (C5)

Pest exclusion features: (1) all gaps >6 mm in the building envelope sealed; (2) ventilation openings screened with 6 mm galvanised mesh; (3) all doors have rubber or brush seals at threshold and jambs; (4) drainage openings covered with SS mesh inserts; (5) no internal ledges >50 mm depth without ≥45° slope; (6) equipment on feet to eliminate floor-level harbourage. Inspected by licensed technician every 6 months.
5.3 Waste Disposal Design (C6)

Floor drainage in the processing area consists of an open channel (150 mm wide × 100 mm deep) running to an outlet at the building perimeter. The outlet discharges via a short pipe to the site's agricultural drainage channel which runs to the property boundary. No sump, interceptor trap or containment is provided between the processing floor drain and the external waterway.
6. WASTE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — Element 3.1 checking point C7
6.1 Waste Management Procedures (C7)

Waste Control System (Doc WCS-001): defines (a) waste stream classification, (b) daily/weekly/post-production cleaning tasks, (c) responsible personnel, (d) waste contractor schedule, (e) emergency spill response. Compliance records in digital operations log. Internal audit quarterly.
Waste streams and handling arrangements:
7. ESTABLISHMENT CONDITION
Rules s4-6 — Element 3.4 (C8) and Element 3.5 (C9)
7.1 Hygiene and Cleanliness (C8)

Establishment condition — most recent internal inspection: processing hall floor clean, drains clear; grading equipment wiped down post-use, no residue on contact surfaces; wall linings free from dust and condensation staining; chemical store tidy with labelled containers; waste bins emptied and clean. Condition consistent with good hygiene practices.
7.2 Pest Condition (C9)

Establishment pest-free: no rodent activity (no droppings, gnaw marks or runs observed); insect pheromone traps — current catches below threshold (3 moths/week vs 10 moths/week threshold); grain probe sampling negative for live insects; bird deterrents in place and effective; all bait stations serviceable.

HYGIENE & SANITATION MANAGEMENT PLAN
Registered Establishment — Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021
1. ESTABLISHMENT INFORMATION
2. SCOPE AND OBJECTIVES
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — System of controls to manage hygiene and waste at the establishment

This plan covers all areas of Nhill Grain Services used in grain handling and storage operations for export Canola. It applies to all permanent and casual employees, contractors, and visitors on site. The plan is reviewed annually or following any significant change to the establishment or operations.
Objectives of this plan:
Ensure all areas of the establishment are maintained in a clean and hygienic condition.
Prevent contamination of Canola during handling and export preparation.
Establish clear responsibilities for cleaning activities.
Maintain records that demonstrate ongoing compliance with hygiene requirements.
Support effective pest exclusion through hygienic site conditions.
3. PERSONNEL AND RESPONSIBILITIES
4. MASTER CLEANING SCHEDULE
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — documented system of controls for hygiene (C1, C2)
5. AREA-SPECIFIC CLEANING PROCEDURES (SOPs)
Detailed step-by-step procedures for each area of the establishment
Receival Pit / Weighbridge

Pre-receival: Inspect pit and scale platform for residual grain from previous lot. Activate compressed air lance to dislodge grain from crevices, joints and conveyor housings. Sweep accumulated grain into collection bin. Wipe scale display and control panel with damp cloth. Supervisor to sign pre-loading checklist before grain intake commences.
Elevator Boot & Leg Casings

At end of each operating day: Lock out elevator drive before opening access hatch. Using industrial vacuum, extract all dead-stock grain from boot throat, casing joints, and transition points. Inspect internal surfaces for grain bridges or insect webbing. Record any pest signs in the Pest Monitoring Log. Replace and secure access hatch. Enter completed task in Equipment Cleaning Log.
Belt Conveyors & Augers

Weekly maintenance cleaning: Isolate drive motor and lock out before commencing. Run conveyor empty for five minutes to clear carrying strand. Remove belt guards and clean all carry rollers and return rollers with a stiff brush. Vacuum accumulated grain and dust from trough pan. Inspect belt splice and edges for wear. Reassemble all guards before returning to service. Record in Cleaning Log.
Grain Storage Silos / Bins

Between commodity lots: Full physical inspection and clean-out required before loading a new grain lot. Access silo through roof hatch or side door (confined space procedure applies). Sweep-out all surfaces using long-handled broom. Vacuum residue from cone and floor. Inspect walls and roof for webbing, insect activity, or mould. Record findings on Pre-Loading Checklist. Silo must not be loaded until the checklist is signed by the Storage Manager.
Grain Screening / Cleaning Plant

Designated staff are responsible for maintaining the Grain Screening / Cleaning Plant in a clean and hygienic condition following each production run or daily as scheduled. Appropriate cleaning agents at specified dilutions shall be used. Completed cleaning activities are to be recorded in the site cleaning log.
6. MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUES AND DEAD-STOCK ZONES

Particular attention is given to dead-stock zones in elevator boots, conveyor transition points, and auger troughs. These areas accumulate grain that cannot self-clear during normal operation and provide harbouring conditions for stored product insects. Full physical extraction is required at each lot change.
7. APPROVED CLEANING CHEMICAL REGISTER
All chemicals must be used at specified dilutions. Safety Data Sheets (SDS) maintained on site.
8. RECORD-KEEPING SYSTEM
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — records to demonstrate compliance (C3, C4)
8.1 Record System

The establishment operates a digital hygiene management system (AgriCompliance Pro) for recording all cleaning activities. Paper originals are scanned and archived within 48 hours. Records are retained for a minimum of two years and are available for audit on request.
8.2 Sanitation Verification Log Template
9. VERIFICATION PROCEDURES
A trained quality officer conducts spot verification checks on a rotating schedule covering all areas within each working week. Verification findings are recorded in the Quality Inspection Register.
10. NON-CONFORMANCE AND CORRECTIVE ACTION

If a cleaning check reveals an area is not compliant with this plan, the area is isolated and re-cleaned. The supervisor completes a Corrective Action Report within 24 hours. The report is reviewed by management and used to update training or procedures where required.
11. ESTABLISHMENT CONDITION ASSESSMENT
Rules s4-6 — establishment to be maintained in a condition appropriate for export operations (C5)

The internal inspection conducted on 30 March 2025 identified product residue accumulation at the base of the elevator boot and under the belt conveyor transfer points. The areas were scheduled for additional cleaning. A follow-up inspection date is to be confirmed with the site manager.
